Rashi on Shabbat 114a:10:1.hebrew: חלבי שבת - כגון אברי תמיד של בין הערבים, קריבים במוצאי שבת, והוא יום הכפורים:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:10:1.english: The fats of Shabbat - For example, the limbs of the afternoon daily burnt-offering [are] offered at the conclusion of Shabbat, which is Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:10:2.hebrew: עולת שבת בשבתו - משמע למידרש בלא וי"ו, ומשמע דעולת שבת קריבה בשבת אחרת — לימד על חלבי שבת כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:10:2.english: The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat - [This] implies [that one should] expound [the word] without [the] vav, and [thus] it implies that the burnt-offering of Shabbat is offered on another Shabbat — [as the baraita states:] "it taught regarding the fats of Shabbat, etc."

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:10:3.hebrew: יכול אף של יוה"כ בשבת ת"ל בשבתו - וי"ו מיעוטו הוא: בשבתו, ולא בשבת אחרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:10:3.english: One might [have thought] even [the fats] of Yom Kippur [are offered] on Shabbat; therefore the verse states, “on its Shabbat” - The [letter] vav is its limitation: “on its Shabbat,” and not on another Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:11:1.hebrew: שקריבים בי"ט - שחל להיות במוצאי שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:11:1.english: That are offered on a Festival - That falls at the conclusion of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:12:1.hebrew: נדרים ונדבות - פלוגתא היא במסכת ביצה (דף יט.), ור' ישמעאל סבירא ליה כמאן דאמר קריבין. הלכך, כיון דנדרים ונדבות — שיכול להמתין ולשחטן בחול ולהקריבן — נשחטים ונקרבין ביום טוב, קל וחומר בחלבי שבת שנשחטו כדרכן בזמנן וניתותרו. הלכך, לא איצטריך קרא "עולת שבת בשבתו" אלא ליום הכפורים:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:12:1.english: Vows and free-will offerings - It is a dispute in Tractate Beitzah (19a), and Rabbi Yishmael holds like the one who says they are offered [on a Festival]. Therefore, since vows and free-will offerings — which one can wait and slaughter on a weekday and offer them — are slaughtered and offered on a Festival, all the more so [is this true] regarding the fats of Shabbat, which were slaughtered in their normal manner in their [proper] time and were left over. Therefore, the verse "the burnt offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat" is only needed for Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:1.english: From where [is it derived regarding] changing clothes - [That] it is a matter of honor before the Omnipresent.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:2.hebrew: ולבש בגדים אחרים - והוציא את הדשן, הזקיקו הכתוב ללבוש בגדים פחותים בשעת הוצאת הדשן, שאינה עבודה חשובה, כדי שלא ימאסו בגדיו החשובים שעובד בהן עבודת אכילה ושתיה, כגון קיטור וניסוך:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:2.english: And he shall don other garments - "and he shall bring out the ashes" — Scripture required him to wear inferior garments at the time of bringing out the ashes, which is not an important service, so that his important garments, in which he performs the service of eating and drinking — such as burning [offerings] and pouring libations — will not become soiled.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:3.hebrew: ותנא דבי ר' ישמעאל - בדרשא דהאי קרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:3.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught - In the exposition of this verse.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:4.english: Clothes in which he cooked a pot [of food] for his master - Similar to the removal of the ashes.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:1:5.english: He should not pour a cup for his master in them - Therefore, he was required to wear inferior garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:1.english: A fat stain - Fat and tallow.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:2.english: Liable to death - For he must be esteemed and respectable for the honor of his Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:3.hebrew: משניאי - שממאסין עצמן בעיני הבריות, והבריות אומרים: "אוי להם ללומדי התורה, שהם מאוסים ומגונים". נמצא זה משניא את התורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:3.english: Those who cause Me to be hated - For they make themselves repulsive in the eyes of people, and people say: "Woe to those who study the Torah, for they are repulsive and despicable." Thus, this [person] causes the Torah to be hated.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:4.hebrew: רבד איתמר - שכבת זרע. לשון ״מרבדים רבדתי ערשי״ (משלי ז׳:ט״ז) — ריפדתיו וקישטתיו בבשמים, מינים המכניסים תאוה, ותזקק לי:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:4.english: Revad was stated - [A stain of] semen. [It is] an expression [like] "I have decked my couch with coverlets [marvadim ravadti arsi]" (Proverbs 7:16) — I have spread it and adorned it with spices, kinds [of things] that arouse lust, so that you will be joined to me.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:5.english: On a cloak - which is an outer [garment], even a fat stain [renders him liable].

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:6.hebrew: בלבוש - שהוא תחתון, רבד אין, רבב לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:3:6.english: On a garment - Which is an undergarment: [a stain of] semen [revad] — yes; [a stain of] grease [revav] — no.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:5:1.hebrew: תנן התם - במסכת מקוואות. ונקט לה משום דבעי למימר "של בנאים כו'", לומר שדרך תלמיד חכם מקפיד על לבושיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:5:1.english: We learned there - In tractate Mikvaot. And [the Gemara] cited it because it wants to state, "[A garment] of builders, etc.," to say that the way of a Torah scholar [is that he] is particular about his garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:5:2.english: On the saddle - Of a donkey.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:5:3.hebrew: חוצץ - כל דבר חוצץ לענין טבילה, דקפיד עליה, וכל חציצה שמקפיד עליו חוצצת:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:5:3.english: Interposes - Every [such] thing interposes with respect to [ritual] immersion, for one is particular about it, and any interposition that one is particular about interposes.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:5:4.english: On both sides - That there was a lot of it, until it was absorbed into the garment and became visible on the other side.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:6:1.hebrew: מרדעת מצד אחד או מב' צדדין - לר' ישמעאל דאמר בבגד מצד אחד, מרדעת מאי אמר בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:6:1.english: A saddle, on one side or on two sides - According to Rabbi Yishmael, who says regarding a garment [that a stain] on one side [constitutes an interposition], what does he say regarding a saddle?

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:6:2.hebrew: ר' יוסי אומר של בנאים - פליג אדר' יהודה, ואמר לר' ישמעאל: בגד של בנאים — דהיינו תלמידי חכמים שמקפידין על לבושיהן — מצד אחד, ושל בור מב' צדדין:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:6:2.english: Rabbi Yosei says: [That] of builders - He disagrees with Rabbi Yehudah, and says to Rabbi Yishmael: A garment of builders — that is, Torah scholars, who are particular about their clothing — [interposes] on one side, and [that] of an ignoramus, on two sides.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:7:1.hebrew: שמחזירים לו אבדה בטביעת עין - כיון שאמר אני מכירה, אע"פ שאינו נותן בה סימן, כדאמר באלו מציאות (ב"מ כג:):
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:7:1.english: That one returns a lost object to him based on visual identification - Once he says, "I recognize it," even though he does not provide an identifying sign for it, as is stated in [the chapter] Eilu Metziot (Bava Metzia 23b).

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:7:2.hebrew: המקפיד על חלוקו להופכו - לובשו כשהוא הפוך, מקפיד עליו והופכו, שמקפיד עליו שלא יראו התפירות המגונות ואימרי החלוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:7:2.english: Who is particular about his shirt to turn it [right-side out] - [If] he puts it on while it is inside out, he is particular about it and turns it [right-side out], for he is particular about it so that the unsightly seams and the hems of the shirt will not be seen.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:7:3.hebrew: בכל מקום - בכל הש"ס, ואפי' במסכת כלה דלא רגילי בה אינשי, וזה נתן לבו וגרסה. מסכת כלה ברייתא היא: "כלה בלא ברכה אסורה לבעלה כנדה":
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:7:3.english: In every place - Throughout the entire Talmud, and even in Tractate Kalla, with which people are not familiar, yet this [scholar] set his mind [to it] and learned it. Tractate Kalla is a baraita [that begins]: "A bride without a blessing is forbidden to her husband like a menstruant [niddah]."

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:8:1.hebrew: ת"ח שבני עירו מצווין לעשות מלאכתו - כדאמר בפרק ז' דיומא (דף עב:), כתוב א' אומר "ועשית לך ארון עץ", וכתוב אחד אומר "ועשו ארון עצי שטים" וגו':
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:8:1.english: A Torah scholar for whom the inhabitants of his city are commanded to perform his labor - As it says in the seventh chapter of Yoma (72b): One verse states, "And you shall make for yourself an ark of wood," and one verse states, "And they shall make an ark of acacia wood," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:8:2.english: To exert [themselves] for his bread - Something that he cannot exert himself for, and [upon which] his life depends.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:8:3.hebrew: אם יודע להשיב במסכת שהוא עוסק בה, ממנים אותו פרנס באתריה:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:8:3.english: If he knows how to answer [questions] in the tractate that he is studying, they appoint him as a leader in his place.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:8:4.english: And if in all of his learning - For he is [engaged] in this tractate and answers [questions] in another tractate.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:9:1.hebrew: אלו כלים האוליירין - הא דתנן בנאין מצד אחד, היינו כלים של אוליירין — בלנים שיש להם אלונטיאות חשובות להתעטף בהם בני אדם חשובים בצאתם מן המרחץ — ומקפידים על טינוף מעט. ובנאים — לשון בי בני (לעיל שבת דף לג:):
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:9:1.english: These are the garments of the ulairin - That which we learned [in the Mishnah], “banna’in on one side,” refers to the garments of ulairin — bathhouse attendants who have fine towels for important people to wrap themselves in when they leave the bathhouse — and they are particular about [even] a slight stain. And banna’im is [derived from] the expression bei banei [bathhouse] (above, Shabbat 33b).

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:9:2.hebrew: למימרא דחיורי נינהו - מדמקפידין על רבב שעליהם, דאילו סומקי לא מיגנו בטינוף פורתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 114a:9:2.english: Is that to say that they are white - Since they are particular about a stain upon them, whereas if [they were] red, they would not be disgraced by a little bit of dirt.

Rashi on Shabbat 114a:9:3.english: Lest I not be acquitted - and I will sit among those who are judged in Gehinnom, who resemble the bottom of a pot.

Tosafot on Shabbat 114a:10:1.hebrew: חלבי שבת קריבין ביוה"כ - אומר ר"י דכל היכא דקתני תרי שבי דהוו בהדי הדדי, אתיא כאחרים דאמרי: אין בין עצרת לעצרת אלא ד' ימים בלבד; והכי מפרש הש"ס בפ' בתרא דסוכה (דף נד:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 114a:10:1.english: The fats of Shabbat are offered on Yom Kippur - Ri says that wherever [the Talmud] teaches [a case of] two Shabbats [i.e., Shabbat and Yom Kippur] that are adjacent to one another, it follows Acherim, who say: There are only four days between [one] Atzeret [Shavuot] and [the next] Atzeret; and so the Talmud explains in the last chapter of Sukkah (54b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 114a:3:1.hebrew: הא בלבושא הא בגלימא - הא דר' ינאי בגלימא, כדמשמע בפ' כל היד (נדה דף כ.) גבי "שחור כחרת": "ור' יוחנן אמר: אלו כלים האוליירין הבאין ממדינת הים. למימרא דאוכמי נינהו? והאמר ר' ינאי כו'. לא קשיא: הא בגלימא, הא בפתורי" — דר' ינאי בגלימא, דהיא סומקי, דשחורים לא הוו, כדמסיק הכא; אבל פתורי הוו אוכמי, ולבושא חיורי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 114a:3:1.english: This [refers] to an undergarment [levusha], [and] this [refers] to an overgarment [gelima] - That [statement] of Rabbi Yannai [refers] to an overgarment [gelima], as is implied in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaYad (Niddah 20a) regarding "black like ink": "And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: These are the cloths of the bath attendants [ha'olyarin] that come from overseas. Is that to say that they are black? But didn't Rabbi Yannai say, etc.? [This is] not difficult: this [refers] to an overgarment [gelima], [and] this [refers] to tablecloths [petorei]." — For Rabbi Yannai's [statement refers] to an overgarment [gelima], which is red [sumkei], for they are not black, as it concludes here; however, tablecloths [petorei] are black, and undergarments [levusha] are white.

Tosafot on Shabbat 114a:7:1.hebrew: ואפילו במסכת כלה - פי' בקונט' דלא רגילי בה אינשי, והוא נתן בלבו לגורסה. ובקדושין פי' לגריעותא, בפרק האיש מקדש (קידושין דף מט:) גבי "ע"מ שאני תלמיד": "אין אומרים כשמעון בן עזאי וכשמעון בן זומא, אלא כל ששואלין אותו דבר הלכה ואפי' במסכת כלה", ופי' בקונטרס: "אפי' במס' כלה שהיא קלה". ונראה דהכא משמע (ואומר) דנקט ליה משום חשיבות — שיודע אפי' במסכת כלה דלא רגילי בה אינשי, ראוי למנותו פרנס; אבל התם קתני "דבר אחד מתלמודו", משמע אפי' לא למד אלא מסכת כלה ואמר הימנה דבר אחד, הרי זה חכם. ומיהו בפירוש רש"י דקידושין, וכן בפי' רבינו חננאל, אין כתוב בהן "דבר אחד מתלמודו". ורבינו יצחק מפרש דהאי "מסכת כלה" היינו דרשות הסדורות מהלכות החג, כדאמרינן בלא יחפור (ב"ב כב.): "רב נחמן בר יצחק ריש כלה הוה"; וקאמר איזהו ת"ח שראוי למנותו על הציבור באתריה — כדאמר בסמוך "במסכתי' באתריה" — כגון שיודע להשיב בכל מקום שישאלוהו באותה מסכת, אפי' במס' כלה שרגילין בה, ראוי למנותו בעירו; אבל בציר מהכי אין ראוי למנותו. והא דהוצרך לחזור ולהשמיענו בסמוך "אי במסכתיה באתריה", אע"ג דכבר השמיענו כאן — לפי שרוצה לחלק בין מסכת לכוליה הש"ס; והשתא הוי דהכא כי ההוא דקידושין (דף מט:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 114a:7:1.english: And even in Tractate Kalla - Rashi explained that people are not accustomed to [studying] it, yet he set his heart to review it. And in Kiddushin, [Rashi] explained [it] in a derogatory sense, in the chapter HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 49b), regarding [the case of one who betroths a woman] "on condition that I am a scholar": "We do not say [he must be] like Shimon ben Azzai or like Shimon ben Zoma; rather, anyone whom they ask a matter of halakha [and he answers], even in Tractate Kalla," and Rashi explained [there]: "even in Tractate Kalla, which is easy." And it appears that here [the Gemara] implies (and he answers) that it mentions it because of [its] importance — that since he knows even Tractate Kalla, which people are not accustomed to [studying], he is fit to be appointed a community leader; whereas there [in Kiddushin], [the Baraita] teaches "one matter from his Talmud," [which] implies [that] even if he only studied Tractate Kalla and stated one matter from it, behold, he is [considered] a scholar. However, in Rashi's commentary to Kiddushin, and likewise in Rabbeinu Chananel's commentary, "one matter from his Talmud" is not written in them. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak explains that this "Tractate Kalla" refers to the discourses arranged from the laws of the festival, as we say in [the chapter] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 22a): "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was Reish Kalla"; and [the Gemara here] is saying: Who is a Torah scholar who is fit to be appointed over the community in his place — as it says shortly [below]: "in his tractate, in his place" — for example, one who knows how to respond in any place where they ask him in that tractate, even in Tractate Kalla with which they are familiar, is fit to be appointed in his city; but less than this, he is not fit to be appointed. And that which it needed to repeat and teach us shortly [below], "if in his tractate, in his place," even though it already taught us [this] here — [is] because it wants to distinguish between [mastery of] one tractate and the entire Talmud; and now [the statement] here is like that [statement] in Kiddushin (49b).
